summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (Oct 2021 - Jan 2022), all already recorded as award rows. Adds 6 denial case rows (other claimants and a related-action claim denied in Releases 93414, 93636 (2), 93637, 93726, 93812) and 44 suggested corrections giving each award's reasons, reductions (delay, culpability, limited assistance), joint/related-action structure and contest status; one correction flags that Release 93637 paid two whistleblowers, not one. No statistics, new rules or new events: rule restatements (30% presumption, TCR waiver, related actions under DOJ agreements, receiver distributions) are already recorded. Insider status is not stated in these orders beyond culpability findings.

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 93286, File No. 2022-4. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 12, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "almost $1.3 million": upper bound; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Significant information prompted the opening of the investigation; multiple interviews; continued helpful information over a two year period. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for information that prompted the investigation, with interviews and two years of continued help.

Exchange Act Release No. 93340, File No. 2022-6. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 15, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $300,000" (current payout across two covered actions): lower bound; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Claimant alerted staff, prompting the investigation; significant ongoing assistance helped shut down an ongoing fraudulent scheme. No denials stated. Both covered actions and sanctions redacted.
Award on two covered actions for a tip that opened the investigation and helped shut down an ongoing fraud.

Exchange Act Release No. 93370, File No. 2022-7. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 18, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $400,000"; percentage redacted. Not contested (through counsel). The Rule 21F-6(c) presumption of the maximum 30% award did not apply because two negative factors were present: unreasonable reporting delay (tip submitted about four years after the claimant became aware of the misconduct, while investors continued to be harmed) and culpability (Claimant, in a redacted role, facilitated the misconduct, e.g. by trying to hide it). Staff were unaware of the misconduct until the tip. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award reduced below the maximum for a culpable claimant who waited about four years to report.

Exchange Act Release No. 93414, File No. 2022-8. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 25, 2021). Joint award to Claimant 1 and Claimant 2, paid 50% each unless they jointly request otherwise. Amount as printed: "more than $1.5 million" (total payout): lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Several proceedings treated as a single covered action (same nucleus of operative facts); claims on a further related covered action treated as timely given the unrepresented claimants' clear intention to apply. Spoke with staff after submitting tips; information on breadth of wrongdoing, other parties and witness credibility. A third claimant was denied (separate row). Covered actions and sanctions redacted.
Joint award to two unrepresented claimants across covered actions treated as one; a third claimant denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 93440, File No. 2022-9. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 28, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $24,000"; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Substantial assistance (in-person meeting, documents, potential witnesses) enabled the Commission to bring an emergency action. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted; several redacted passages.
Award for assistance that enabled the Commission to bring an emergency action.

Exchange Act Release No. 93441, File No. 2022-10. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 28, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $750,000"; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Claimant alerted the Commission to ongoing conduct, prompting the investigation; multiple voluntary interviews, key witnesses, documents and explanations of complex issues saved staff time. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for a tip on ongoing conduct that opened the investigation, with substantial continued help.

Exchange Act Release No. 93465, File No. 2022-11. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 29, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Related-action award: the award is on sanctions in a related action resolved by the DOJ through a (redacted type of) agreement, treated as an administrative action under Rule 21F-4(d)(3)(i) as amended effective 7 Dec 2020. Claimant had previously received an award in the SEC covered action (redacted). Amount as printed: "more than $2,000,000": lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Same original information given to DOJ and SEC prompted both investigations; extensive ongoing assistance. No denials stated.
Related-action award on a DOJ agreement, to a claimant already awarded in the SEC action.

Exchange Act Release No. 93635, File No. 2022-17. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 22, 2021). Claimant 1 as named in the order (joint claimants collectively called Claimant 1, paid 50% each unless they request otherwise): aggregate award "more than $240,000": lower bound, across the SEC covered action and a related action by another (redacted) agency; percentages redacted. Not contested. Tip in part prompted the investigation; met staff and the other agency. Equal percentage with Claimant 2 in the covered action; higher percentage than Claimant 2 in the related action because Claimant 1's information played a more significant role there. Covered action, related action and sanctions redacted.
Joint award (covered and related action) to claimants whose tip helped open the investigation.

Exchange Act Release No. 93635, File No. 2022-17. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 22, 2021). Claimant 2 as named in the order: aggregate award "approximately $195,000", across the SEC covered action and a related action by another (redacted) agency; percentages redacted. Not contested. New, detailed and highly valuable information early in the investigation, instrumental to the theory of liability; met staff and the other agency. Same percentage as Claimant 1 in the covered action, lower in the related action. Covered action, related action and sanctions redacted.
Award (covered and related action) for early information that shaped the theory of liability.

Exchange Act Release No. 93636, File No. 2022-15. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 22, 2021). Claimant 1 as named in the order: "more than $6.2 million" (covered action plus a related action by redacted "Other Agencies" together): lower bound; percentages redacted. Contest status not stated. New information during an existing investigation; all of it corroborated and the majority of the relief was based on Claimant 1's allegations; reported internally first and reported to the Commission expeditiously. Claimant 2 (separate row) and Claimant 3 denials in footnote 2 (separate rows). Covered action, related action and sanctions redacted.
Larger of two awards (covered and related action) for information behind most of the relief; reported internally first.

Exchange Act Release No. 93636, File No. 2022-15. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 22, 2021). Claimant 2 as named in the order: "more than $1.3 million" based on current collections, covered action only: lower bound; percentage redacted. New information during an existing investigation on schemes in a different geographic area; substantial assistance; waited approximately 16 months before reporting to the Commission. Claimant 2's related-action claim was denied (separate row). Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Smaller award for a claimant who waited about 16 months to report; related-action claim denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 93637, File No. 2022-16. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 22, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 2 (Claimant 1 and Claimant 2, separate redacted percentages; Claimant 2's is described as significantly lower). Amount as printed: "approximately $2.4 million" is the anticipated combined initial payment to both claimants based on current collections; no per-claimant amounts. Claimant 1 contested, arguing Claimant 2 was ineligible or Claimant 1 deserved more; the Commission rejected this and adopted the CRS recommendations. Claimant 1's information caused the investigation to open; Claimant 2 provided new information of substantially less value. Two other claimants denied (separate row). Covered action, judgments and sanctions redacted.
Combined initial payment to two claimants; Claimant 1's contest for a larger share rejected; two other claimants denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 93648, File No. 2022-18. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Nov. 23, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "almost $400,000", across the covered action and a related action by a redacted authority: upper bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Form TCR filed within two weeks of learning of the requirement, satisfying the waiver in new Rule 21F-9(e). Award reduced for culpability (claimant not charged), with mitigating factors (some harmed investors were connected to the claimant; unaware of some fraudulent aspects; helped remediate). Helped shut down an ongoing Ponzi-like scheme on retail investors and obtain emergency relief; money returned to harmed investors. Receiver distributions to injured investors treated as collected sanctions; no collections to date in the related action. No denials stated.
Award reduced for culpability, on a Ponzi-like scheme; TCR filing requirement met under the new 30-day waiver rule.

Exchange Act Release No. 93685, File No. 2022-19. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Dec. 1, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $175,000" across two covered actions: lower bound; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Original information was independent analysis of publicly available information (calculations revealing violations not apparent from public materials). The Rule 21F-6(c) presumption of the 30% maximum did not apply because of "limited assistance": the tip was one of several that contributed to opening the investigation and the claimant gave no further information or assistance. Receiver distributions to harmed investors treated as collected sanctions. No denials stated. Covered actions and sanctions redacted.
Award below the maximum for independent analysis of public information; tip was one of several and no further help given.

Exchange Act Release No. 93726, File No. 2022-20. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Dec. 7, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $4.9 million" (current award): lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Reported quickly on suspected misuse of securities offering proceeds; two interviews and financial documents; helped return millions of dollars to harmed investors. Receiver distributions may be counted as collected sanctions (footnote 1). A second claimant denied (separate row). Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for a prompt report of misused offering proceeds; a second claimant denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 93812, File No. 2022-21. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Dec. 17, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Amount as printed: "more than $900,000": lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Tip with documents and analysis caused the investigation to open; further communications through counsel; money returned to harmed investors. Claimant 2 denied after contesting (separate row). Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for a tip with documents and analysis that opened the investigation; a second claimant denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 93913, File No. 2022-22. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 6, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over $13 million" (total award): lower bound; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Expeditiously reported an ongoing fraud, prompting the investigation; met staff in person, explained the scheme and prepared a declaration supporting emergency relief; helped shut down the fraud and return tens of millions of dollars to harmed investors. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for a prompt tip and declaration that helped stop an ongoing fraud and return tens of millions to investors.

Exchange Act Release No. 93935, File No. 2022-23. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 10, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $2.6 million"; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Reported internally first; information significantly contributed to an existing investigation, revealing unknown misconduct and helping obtain evidence of wrongdoing abroad; identified witnesses. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award to a claimant who reported internally first and helped obtain evidence of wrongdoing abroad.

Exchange Act Release No. 93936, File No. 2022-24. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 10, 2022). Joint award to Claimant 1 and Claimant 2, paid 50% each unless they jointly request otherwise. Amount as printed: "approximately $1.5 million" (total payout); percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Several interviews and numerous calls with staff through counsel, including around key witness testimony. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Joint award to two claimants for substantial ongoing assistance through counsel.

Exchange Act Release No. 93945, File No. 2022-26. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 11, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30% (statutory maximum under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption: maximum award would not exceed $5 million, no negative factors, more than limited assistance). "There also have been minimal collections to date in the matter." Contest status not stated. Tip in part prompted a new investigation into an ongoing fraud; testimony and numerous documents. No denials stated. Covered action redacted.
Maximum 30% award under the presumption for awards up to $5 million; minimal collections so far.

Exchange Act Release No. 93946, File No. 2022-25. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 11, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30% (statutory maximum under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption). "There have been no collections to date in this matter." Contest status not stated. Important new information prompted the investigation; voluntary interviews; certain charges directly based on Claimant's information. No denials stated. Covered action redacted.
Maximum 30% award under the presumption for awards up to $5 million; nothing collected yet.

Exchange Act Release No. 93947, File No. 2022-27. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 11, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $450,000": lower bound; percentage redacted. Contest status not stated. Important new information prompted the investigation; voluntary interviews and voluminous documents; charges based in significant part on the information. No denials stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award for new information that opened the investigation and shaped the charges.
